notes.decision: Translated 'she is forever' — the predication of eternal duration to a feminine entity (likely Matter/Hyle bound in the bōlos). The construction is OY-(noun)-ⲧⲉ + ϣⲁⲁⲛⲏϩⲉ 'unto eternity.'
Read as ⲁ-ⲧ-ⲙⲣⲡⲉ 'into the bond,' where ⲙⲣⲡⲉ is a Lycopolitan variant of ⲙⲣ̄ⲣⲉ 'bond, fetter.' Confirmed by line 8 ⲟⲩⲙⲣⲡⲉ ⲧⲉ ϣⲁⲁⲛⲏϩⲉ 'she is a bond forever.'

Translated 'the middle' — taking ⳨ here as orthographic variant of ⲧ (definite article), giving ⲧⲙⲏⲧⲉ. Elsewhere on the page ⳨ functions as ϯ ('5') in ⲡ⳨ⲟⲩ; the dialect is inconsistent in its use of this character.
ⲧⲟⲓⲛⲉⲓ 'the coming' (action-noun from ⲉⲓ 'come,' per accumulated vocabulary) + ⲙⲡϯⲟⲩ ⲛ̄ⲱⲧ 'of the Five Fathers' — Lycopolitan ⲱⲧ for ⲉⲓⲱⲧ/ⲓⲱⲧ.

notes.decision: The five-faculty enumeration: mind (ⲛⲟⲩⲥ) → Beloved of the Lights; thought (ⲙⲉⲩⲉ, restored) → Mother of Life; teaching (ⲥⲃⲱ) → [lost title]; counsel (ⲥⲁⲭⲛⲉ) → Virgin of Light/the Beloved; reflection (ⲙⲁⲕⲙⲉⲕ) → [implied closure]. The text places 'the Beloved' (ⲡⲙⲉⲣⲓⲧ) at the line-22 break — likely the entity from teaching, with the Virgin of Light from counsel.
Doubled ⳨ unclear; tentatively read as ⲛ̄†ⲉ or similar — possibly 'in this' (ⲛ̄ϯⲉ) or a corruption. Translated 'in this' modifying ⲟⲓⲛⲉⲓ 'coming.'
Per accumulated vocabulary, ⲡⲧⲭⲁⲓ̈ = 'the abode' (tentative) — distinct from ⲡⲭⲁⲓ̈ 'the world.' Used here as a third item of comparison in the chapter title alongside First Man and Ambassador.

Tentatively rendered 'set out after / pursue.' The construction ⲥⲁ 'after' parallels line 32 ⲉⲓ ⲥⲁ 'came after,' suggesting a verb of pursuit. ⲁ⳨ⲟⲩⲁⲓ̈ may be ⲁⲣⲟⲩⲱ/ⲁⲣⲟⲩⲁⲓ̈ 'to occupy oneself with, ply, follow up.'
Tentatively 'to seek them out / to redeem them' — fits the typological context (the father descending after his lost sons). May be Lyc form of ϣⲓⲛⲉ 'seek' or ⲥⲱⲧⲉ 'redeem' with 3pl object suffix.
